_metadata.rubric: x02 rubric (owner style examples, clicks-when-explained bar, fewer phrase-joins, mechanism labelled, explanation checked), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and x02e-revision-review-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: UNICORN via the narwhal's well-known 'unicorn of the sea' nickname and spiral horn; TOOTH via the true fact that the 'horn' is an elongated tooth (a tusk), which gives a satisfying 'oh, nice' once explained.

best_available.why: Both routes are accurate and natural, the unicorn side is instantly guessable, and the tooth fact lands as a genuine reveal; the explanation is brief and correct.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent fact-based hint of exactly the kind the owner wants more of; no phrase-join involved.

hints.reason: ELVIS via Graceland in Memphis, Tennessee; PYRAMID via the ancient Egyptian capital Memphis near the pyramids (and Memphis's own giant Pyramid arena), a double route that feels clever and is factually sound.

best_available.why: A place hint that bridges a U.S. pop-culture icon and ancient Egypt through one name; both sides are accurate and widely known, and the bonus Memphis Pyramid detail reinforces the link.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair. The explanation stacks three facts and runs slightly long against the 'brief' guidance, but every claim is correct and it reads naturally, so no fix is required.

hints.reason: DOOR via knocking on a door; JOKE via the knock-knock joke, and the explanation fuses them into one scene (the joke pretends someone is at your door), so it is a natural, instantly clicking hint rather than a mechanical fill-in.

best_available.why: The most natural hint for the pair: universally known on both sides, PG, and the one-idea explanation is short and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: The JOKE side leans on the compound 'knock-knock joke', so this sits near the phrase-join line; labelled scene because the hint works as one combined image of knocking at a door. Even judged as a phrase-join it would qualify as exceptional (both uses instantly familiar). Delight is modest because it is very easy.
